31700-reflections-of-a-bachelor-girl.title: Reflections Of A Bachelor Girl
31700-reflections-of-a-bachelor-girl.creator: Unknown
31700-reflections-of-a-bachelor-girl.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. imony; but, after all, the shine on a jewel is the whole thing. A MAN firmly believes that, if he can only keep his wife in the straight and narrow path, he can go out and zig-zag all over the downward one without falling from grace. A GIRL is never so surprised when a man proposes to her as he is. LOVE doesn't really "make the world go 'round," it only makes us so dizzy that everything seems to be going round.

arxiv-2011-01010.title: Causal Campbell-Goodhart’s law and Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2011-01010.creator: Hal Ashton 1 1 Computer Science, University College London, UK ucabha5@ucl.ac.uk
arxiv-2011-01010.description: Abstract Campbell-Goodhart’s law relates to the causal inference error whereby decision-making agents aim to influence variables which are correlated to their goal objective but do not reliably cause it. This is a well known error in Economics and Political Science but not widely labelled in Artificial Intelligence research.

arxiv-2012-13568.title: Towards a Universal Continuous Knowledge Base
arxiv-2012-13568.creator: Gang Chen, Maosong Sun, Yang Liu
arxiv-2012-13568.description: Abstract In artificial intelligence (AI), knowledge is the information required by an intelligent system to accomplish tasks. While traditional knowledge bases use discrete, symbolic representations, detecting knowledge encoded in the continuous representations learned from data has received increasing attention recently.

arxiv-2205-00975.title: A portfolio management of a small RES utility with a Structural Vector Autoregressive model of German electricity markets
arxiv-2205-00975.creator: Katarzyna Maciejowska
arxiv-2205-00975.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Katarzyna Maciejowska. The changes in electricity markets expose RES producers and electricity traders to various risks, among which the price and the volume risk play a very important role. In this research, a portfolio building strategies are presented, which allow to dynamically choose a proportion of electricity traded in different electricity markets (day-ahead and intraday) and hence to optimize the behavior of an utility.

arxiv-2206-02268.title: Characters of solvable groups, Hilbert–Schmidt stability and dense periodic measures
arxiv-2206-02268.creator: Arie Levit and Itamar Vigdorovich
arxiv-2206-02268.description: Abstract . We study the character theory of metabelian and polycyclic groups. It is used to investigate Hilbert–Schmidt stability via the character-theoretic criterion of Hadwin and Shulman. There is a close connection between stability and dynamics of automorphisms of compact abelian groups.

arxiv-2209-12183.title: Slow transport and bound states for spinless fermions with long-range Coulomb interactions on one-dimensional lattices
arxiv-2209-12183.creator: Zhi-Hua Li
arxiv-2209-12183.description: Abstract We study transport and relaxation of spinless fermions with long-range Coulomb interactions at high temperatures through numerical simulations of out-of-equilibrium dynamics. We find that the transport and relaxation are continuously slowing down for increasing coupling V V , and that there is a transition in the type of transport.

arxiv-2308-08870.title: Sensitivity and Dynamic Distance Oracles via Generic Matrices and Frobenius Form
arxiv-2308-08870.creator: Adam Karczmarz, Piotr Sankowski
arxiv-2308-08870.description: Abstract Algebraic techniques have had an important impact on graph algorithms so far. Porting them, e.g., the matrix inverse, into the dynamic regime improved best-known bounds for various dynamic graph problems. In this paper, we develop new algorithms for another cornerstone algebraic primitive, the Frobenius normal form (FNF).

arxiv-2502-11968.title: Theoretical Barriers in Bellman-Based Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2502-11968.creator: Brieuc Pinon, Raphaël Jungers, Jean-Charles Delvenne
arxiv-2502-11968.description: Abstract Reinforcement Learning algorithms designed for high-dimensional spaces often enforce the Bellman equation on a sampled subset of states, relying on generalization to propagate knowledge across the state space. In this paper, we identify and formalize a fundamental limitation of this common approach. Specifically, we construct counterexample problems with a simple structure that this approach fails to exploit.

arxiv-2503-09731.title: Results from an Einstein@Home search for continuous gravitational waves from Cassiopeia A and Vela Jr. using LIGO O2 data
arxiv-2503-09731.creator: Jorge Morales, Jing Ming, Maria Alessandra Papa, Heinz-Bernd Eggenstein, Bernd Machenschalk
arxiv-2503-09731.description: Abstract We conduct two searches for continuous, nearly monochromatic gravitational waves originating from the central compact objects in the supernova remnants Cassiopeia A and Vela Jr. using public LIGO data. The search for Cassiopeia A targets signal frequencies between 20 Hz and 400 Hz; the Vela Jr.

arxiv-2505-05672.title: TeGA: Texture Space Gaussian Avatars for High-Resolution Dynamic Head Modeling
arxiv-2505-05672.creator: Gengyan Li, Paulo Gotardo, Timo Bolkart, Stephan Garbin, Kripasindhu Sarkar, Abhimitra Meka, Alexandros Lattas, Thabo Beeler
arxiv-2505-05672.description: Abstract . Sparse volumetric reconstruction and rendering via 3D Gaussian splatting have recently enabled animatable 3D head avatars that are rendered under arbitrary viewpoints with impressive photorealism. Today, such photoreal avatars are seen as a key component in emerging applications in telepresence, extended reality, and entertainment.

arxiv-2506-18673.title: Asymptotic Expansions of Gaussian and Laguerre Ensembles at the Soft Edge III: Generating Functions
arxiv-2506-18673.creator: Folkmar Bornemann
arxiv-2506-18673.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Folkmar Bornemann. We conclude our work [ 5 , 9 ] on asymptotic expansions at the soft edge for the classical n n -dimensional Gaussian and Laguerre ensembles, now studying the gap-probability generating functions. We show that the correction terms in the asymptotic expansion are multilinear forms of the higher-order derivatives of the leading-order term, with certain rational polynomial coefficients that are independent of the dummy variable.

arxiv-2510-27106.title: Rating Roulette: Self-Inconsistency in LLM-As-A-Judge Frameworks
arxiv-2510-27106.creator: Rajarshi Haldar, Julia Hockenmaier
arxiv-2510-27106.description: Abstract As Natural Language Generation (NLG) continues to be widely adopted, properly assessing it has become quite difficult. Lately, using large language models (LLMs) for evaluating these generations has gained traction, as they tend to align more closely with human preferences than conventional n-gram or embedding-based metrics.

britannica-1911-pole-reginald.description: Article 'Pole, Reginald' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 21), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. of Canterbury, born at Stourton Castle, Staffordshire, was the third son of Sir Richard Pole, Knight of the Garter, and Margaret, countess of Salisbury, a daughter of George, duke of Clarence, and therefore niece of Edward IV. He was intended for the church from his youth; and when seven years old was sent for five years to the grammar school which Colet had founded near the Carthusian monastery at Sheen.

pmc-11692569.title: DESIGN ELEMENTS OF EDUCATIONAL TOYS FOR PATIENTS WITH MILD ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE: A QUALITATIVE STUDY
pmc-11692569.creator: HongFei Jia, YaPing Ding, Ling Zhu
pmc-11692569.description: BackgroundAlzheimer’s disease (AD) is a fatal chronic neurodegenerative disease, and its incidence and mortality rate are closely related to age. Once diagnosed, patients need to take long-term medication, which seriously affects the quality of life of those who are ill.

pmc-12866457.title: Silencing TMEM105 suppresses gastric cancer cell growth and migration via proliferation-associated pathways
pmc-12866457.creator: Behnoosh Nikonezhad, Mobina Shahriarizade, Atefeh Zamani, Mohammad Mahdevar
pmc-12866457.description: BackgroundNumerous studies in the field of cancer indicate that long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) play a significant role in the development and malignancy of various cancers. In this study, the expression changes of TMEM105 in gastric cancer (GC) and its association with malignancy were examined.

pmc-12978822.title: Plant structural biology: Emerging technologies and future biological insights
pmc-12978822.creator: Jonas M. Böhm, Veronica G. Maurino
pmc-12978822.description: SUMMARYPlant structural biology is entering a new era. Advances in cryo‐electron microscopy, tomography, and AI‐based prediction are making it possible to study plant macromolecular machines at near‐atomic resolution, including complexes that long resisted analysis by traditional approaches. Yet, despite these developments, plant proteins remain underrepresented in structural databases, reflecting persistent challenges in sample preparation, in situ imaging, and capturing dynamics.

pmc-13064843.title: Regulations for international non-proprietary name prescribing and substitution, relevant for cross-border ePrescribing and eDispensation services in the European Union
pmc-13064843.creator: Robert Vander Stichele, Joseph Roumier, Dirk Van Nimwegen, Dipak Kalra, Argiris Gkogkidis, Nicole Vegiotti, Yuri Quintana, Petra Wilson
pmc-13064843.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Prescribing by international non-proprietary name (INN) and substitution rules are advocated in the education and practice of rational prescribing, and for cost containment policy. Regulations that restrict or foster INN prescribing and substitution exist in all member states. The aim of this study is to describe the national regulations in European Union (EU) countries, to nation-specific tools for ePrescribing and eDispensation systems based on the standards for Identification of Medicinal Products (IDMP) in the European Health Data Space.

pmc-13108969.title: Oncological Outcomes and Treatment Strategies for Borderline Resectable Hepatocellular Carcinoma Based on the Oncological Resectability Classification
pmc-13108969.creator: Takashi Hamada, Akihiko Soyama, Hajime Matsushima, Ayaka Kinoshita, Kazushige Migita, Hajime Imamura, Shun Nakamura, Ayaka Satoh, Kohki Kurotaki, Tomohiko Adachi, Ryu Sasaki, Hisamitsu Miyaaki, Susumu Eguchi
pmc-13108969.description: BackgroundAlthough hepatic resection is the most effective curative treatment for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) in selected patients, survival outcomes can vary significantly depending on tumor burden and biology. To provide a standardized framework, the oncological resectability classification introduced in 2023 stratifies patients into resectable (R), borderline resectable 1 (BR1), or borderline resectable 2 (BR2).

pmc-13115747.title: Postbiotics and Skeletal Muscle Health: Molecular Mechanisms and Translational Perspectives
pmc-13115747.creator: Matylda Korgiel, Maja Jakoniuk, Kacper Rak, Katarzyna Kler, Emil Paluch
pmc-13115747.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Recent evidence implicates the gut microbiota in muscle physiology and function via the gut–muscle axis, which portrays bidirectional communication between microbial colonies, their metabolites and muscle tissue. Age-related muscle decline, including sarcopenia and muscle atrophy, has been associated with shifts in gut microbiota composition and lower levels of microbial metabolites, such as short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), thereby expanding muscle health research toward microbiota-based therapies.

pmc-13241413.title: Telehealth service use in people with cancer compared to people without cancer: analysis of Patient Experience Surveys in Australia
pmc-13241413.creator: Huah Shin Ng, Ramya Walsan, Reema Harrison, Bogda Koczwara
pmc-13241413.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). PurposeTo compare the prevalence and characteristics associated with telehealth use in people with and without cancer.MethodsCross-sectional study using data from the Australia’s Patient Experience Surveys (2022–2023 and 2023–2024) of all participants aged ≥ 25 years.

pmc-13435438.title: Post-marketing safety profile of bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide: a FAERS pharmacovigilance study with EudraVigilance validation and mechanistic investigation of pancreatitis
pmc-13435438.creator: Yuxin Xie, Yawen Luo, Yinghua Chen, Guoqing Shi, Yihuai He, Xia Liu, Zhiwei Cui, Fan Zou, Chengyu Zhu
pmc-13435438.description: BackgroundBictegravir/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir alafenamide (BIC/FTC/TAF) has demonstrated strong efficacy and favorable tolerability as a first-line HIV treatment. However, there is a lack of long-term safety data from large-scale studies and real-world settings. This study aimed to evaluate the post-marketing safety of BIC/FTC/TAF using the FAERS database, with external validation in EudraVigilance, and to further explore the potential mechanisms underlying the pancreatitis signal.

pmc-13469105.title: CMDPC_OBB: A Large-Scale Image Dataset for Coal Mine Drill Pipe Counting based on Oriented Bounding Box
pmc-13469105.creator: Fukai Zhang, Xiaoran Liu, Haiyan Zhang, Feng Guo, Shan Zhao, Yanmei Zhang, Guan Yuan, Lu Dong, Xu Chen, Zhanqiang Huo
pmc-13469105.description: To address the scarcity of publicly available underground coal mine monitoring image datasets and the challenges of accurate recognition under complex drilling environments, this study constructs a large-scale image dataset for coal mine drill pipe counting based on Oriented Bounding Boxes (CMDPC_OBB).
